title: Upon Waking Up
arabic_text: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَحْيَانَا بَعْدَ مَا أَمَاتَنَا وَإِلَيْهِ النُّشُورُ
transliteration: Alhamdu lillahil-lathee ahyana ba'da ma amatana wa-ilayhin-nushoor
translation: Praise is to Allah who gave us life after having taken it from us (in sleep), and unto Him is the resurrection.
benefits: A short reminder, first thing each day, that life, sleep, and waking are all in God's hands — grounding the whole day in gratitude.

title: In the Evening
arabic_text: أَمْسَيْنَا وَأَمْسَى الْمُلْكُ لِلَّهِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ
transliteration: Amsayna wa amsal-mulku lillah, walhamdu lillah
translation: We have reached the evening and at this very time all sovereignty belongs to Allah, and all praise is for Allah.
benefits: Marks the transition into evening with an acknowledgement that all authority and control belongs to God alone.

title: Before Eating
benefits: A short, easy-to-remember dua said before eating or drinking, turning an everyday act into a remembrance of God.

title: After Eating
arabic_text: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَطْعَمَنِي هَذَا وَرَزَقَنِيهِ مِنْ غَيْرِ حَوْلٍ مِنِّي وَلَا قُوَّةٍ
transliteration: Alhamdu lillahil-lathee at'amanee hatha wa razaqaneehi min ghayri hawlin minnee wa la quwwah
translation: Praise is to Allah who fed me this and provided it for me without any power or might on my part.
benefits: A reminder that provision ultimately comes from God, said as gratitude right after finishing a meal.

title: In Times of Anxiety or Grief
arabic_text: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي عَبْدُكَ ابْنُ عَبْدِكَ ابْنُ أَمَتِكَ، نَاصِيَتِي بِيَدِكَ، مَاضٍ فِيَّ حُكْمُكَ، عَدْلٌ فِيَّ قَضَاؤُكَ
transliteration: Allahumma inni 'abduka ibnu 'abdika ibnu amatika, nasiyati biyadika, madin fiyya hukmuka, 'adlun fiyya qada'uk
translation: O Allah, I am Your servant, son of Your servant, son of Your maidservant. My forelock is in Your hand. Your command over me is forever executed, and Your decree over me is just.
benefits: One of the duas the Prophet (peace be upon him) taught for moments of sadness and worry, affirming trust in God's control and justice.

title: Leaving the Home
arabic_text: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ، تَوَكَّلْتُ عَلَى اللَّهِ، وَلَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ
transliteration: Bismillah, tawakkaltu 'alallah, wa la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah
translation: In the name of Allah, I place my trust in Allah, and there is no power nor might except with Allah.
benefits: Said when stepping out of the house, placing the day's affairs in God's hands before facing the world.

title: In Times of Trial and Hardship
arabic_text: لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنتَ سُبْحَٰنَكَ إِنِّى كُنتُ مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
transliteration: La ilaha illa anta subhanaka inni kuntu minaz-zalimin
translation: There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been among the wrongdoers.
benefits: The dua of Prophet Yunus (Jonah), peace be upon him, cried out from the depths of hardship and answered. The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, taught that no believer calls on Allah with it in any difficulty without being helped — a steadying dua for the harder days of adjusting to a new life and, sometimes, a changed relationship with family or community.

title: For Patience and Steadfastness
arabic_text: رَبَّنَآ أَفْرِغْ عَلَيْنَا صَبْرًۭا وَتَوَفَّنَا مُسْلِمِينَ
transliteration: Rabbana afrigh 'alayna sabran wa tawaffana muslimeen
translation: Our Lord, pour upon us patience and let us die as Muslims [in submission to You].
benefits: A short, direct request for the patience to stay firm — asked for by believers who were themselves under pressure for their faith. Fitting to repeat whenever staying the course feels difficult.

title: For Guidance and Uprightness
translation: O Allah, guide me and make me upright.
benefits: The Prophet, peace be upon him, taught this to his cousin Ali and explained it as asking for two things together: being guided to the right path, and being kept straight and correct — in judgment, speech, and how one treats others — once on it.

title: For Gratitude and Righteous Deeds
arabic_text: رَبِّ أَوْزِعْنِىٓ أَنْ أَشْكُرَ نِعْمَتَكَ ٱلَّتِىٓ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَىَّ وَعَلَىٰ وَٰلِدَىَّ وَأَنْ أَعْمَلَ صَٰلِحًۭا تَرْضَىٰهُ وَأَدْخِلْنِى بِرَحْمَتِكَ فِى عِبَادِكَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
transliteration: Rabbi awzi'nee an ashkura ni'mataka allatee an'amta 'alayya wa 'ala walidayya wa an a'mala salihan tardah, wa adkhilnee birahmatika fee 'ibadika-salihin
translation: My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents, and to do righteous deeds that please You, and admit me by Your mercy among Your righteous servants.
benefits: Prophet Sulayman's (Solomon's) dua, said on noticing a small kindness he might have overlooked — gratitude and good action held together as one request, not two separate goals.

title: For Mercy Upon One's Parents
arabic_text: وَٱخْفِضْ لَهُمَا جَنَاحَ ٱلذُّلِّ مِنَ ٱلرَّحْمَةِ وَقُل رَّبِّ ٱرْحَمْهُمَا كَمَا رَبَّيَانِى صَغِيرًۭا
transliteration: Wakhfid lahuma janahadh-dhulli minar-rahmati wa qur-rabbi irhamhuma kama rabbayanee sagheera
translation: And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy, and say: My Lord, have mercy upon them as they cared for me when I was small.
benefits: A request for good, ordinary care and gentleness toward parents in return for their care in childhood — not tied to their own faith, so it applies just as fully to parents who aren't Muslim as to parents who are.
